description: A file of acceptances of sisakulint (sisakulint/acceptances/v0), which --accept of the CLI reads. An entry matches a finding of a report whose certainty is inconclusive when the rule, the kind (args.kind_id, <rule>.<kind>), the input, key_path, span_text and span_lines of the finding are equal to those of the entry. A matched finding does not set bit 8 of the exit code, and the report keeps the matched finding with the reason of the entry (acceptance in report-v0.json). The line and the column of the place are not compared: lines added above the place do not end the match. These changes do not end the match either: a change of the indentation that all the lines of span_lines have in common, a change of the spaces and tabs at the ends of the lines, and a change of the kind of the line breaks. Any other change of span_text or span_lines, and any change of the key path or of the input of the place, ends the match, and the finding counts toward bit 8 again. A change outside the lines of span_lines that keeps the key path and the input of the place does not end the match.

inconclusive.description: The accepted places of findings whose certainty is inconclusive. Two entries with equal values of the six fields (rule, kind_id, input, key_path, span_text and span_lines) are an error.

rule.description: The ID of a rule that declares kind_id (inconclusive_kinds in the registry of rules).

kind_id.description: The kind of the inconclusive finding: args.kind_id of the inconclusive finding in report-v0.json, <rule>.<kind>, where <rule> is the value of rule and <kind> is an inconclusive kind of the rule.

input.description: The name of the input of the place, as location.file.input of the inconclusive finding in report-v0.json.

key_path.description: As key_path of the inconclusive finding in report-v0.json.

span_text.description: As span_text of the inconclusive finding in report-v0.json.

span_lines.description: As span_lines of the inconclusive finding in report-v0.json.

reason.description: Why a person accepts the place: why the value at the place is not an attacker's, for example. A reason that is empty or white space alone is an error.
